learning: If s-bend line-loss stays at 1.3 or more with the oval holding, the sharp-track gap is the controller's response, not geometry. The next controller change should be kp, kd or line_loss mode, one at a time. If the oval drops below about 14/20 or steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.35 with low max_error, the lighter mass is making the oval jittery and mass should return to 0.7 kg.
notes: Iteration 7 package: the Builder's mass test (0.7 to 0.5 kg) on the iteration 6 geometry, with the controller unchanged so only mass differs from the best-known result (372.2). Measurements add control_effort and controller_errors to read the controller on the lighter robot.
rationale: Iteration 6 (wheel_track 0.09 m, controller unchanged) is the best-known design at 372.2. The oval holds at 17/20 with max_error 0.0435 m and steering_oscillation 0.30, under the 0.35 limit. The sharp tracks have not moved: s-bend line-loss is 1.3 per run with 0/20 finishes, and slalom is 1.9 with 0/20. Span (iteration 2), footprint (iteration 3), forward position (iteration 4) and narrowing (iterations 5 and 6) have each been tested. Speed is not the limit, since the oval finishes in about 1.85 s. Mass is the one body lever not yet tested cleanly, because iteration 0 to 1 changed it together with wheel_track and sensors. Yaw inertia is mass*(L^2+W^2)/12, so lowering mass should ease turning on sharp bends. I accept the Builder's proposal as written: geometry is unchanged except mass 0.7 to 0.5 kg. The controller stays exactly as in iterations 4 to 6 (base_speed 1.2, kp 2.5, ki 0, kd 0.3, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction), so the race isolates mass. Expected result: s-bend line-loss falls toward 1.0 or below and the oval holds at 16/20 or better. Because the controller is unchanged, a flat line-loss result would point to the controller's response on sharp bends, and I would then change kp, kd or the line-loss mode next. I do not expect a large score change.
